cohort: Pregnant mothers and their infants (N=168 breastfed and 31 formula-fed in the probiotic group; N=201 breastfed and 22 formula-fed in the placebo group) who received either probiotic or placebo supplementation.
finding: Probiotic supplementation, especially in conjunction with breastfeeding, can significantly impact infant microbiota composition and function, and can ameliorate the negative effects of antibiotic use and caesarean birth on the gut microbiota.
mod_finding: In the placebo group, caesarean birth was significantly associated with altered microbiota composition and function, particularly reduced Bifidobacterium abundance, but these effects were eliminated or reduced in the probiotic group.
